about: The short state of the project. Read it first; DESIGN.md has the detail and the evidence. Update it when a milestone, a decision or a dead end lands.

autochart's CUDA provider in WSL needs CUDA 13 libraries (the cu132 lane's wheels plus nvidia-curand): it loaded and ran the guitar on the 5070 in M4-00b's spike and in the GPU smoke test; a driver under 580 leaves the guitar on the CPU. VRAM: 8,987 MiB at the peak of 12 GB, and the friend's 4070 has 12 GB with Windows' desktop holding some (M4-08 records the free VRAM)

the Start-menu shortcut under Smart App Control: a .lnk written from WSL has no Mark of the Web and targets the signed wsl.exe, so it should run; untested until M4-08 (fallback: open Ubuntu, type songcharter)
the Windows browser reaches the server through WSL's localhost forwarding (default on); the server checks it from Windows with curl.exe and falls back to WSL's own address
decisions: route: WSL2, not native Windows (the owner, 2026-11-03): the friend's PC has Smart App Control on, which blocks unsigned DLLs and Python modules with no per-app exception; Linux programs in WSL2 are outside it, and onnxruntime-node's Linux build gives the guitar CUDA again

memory rule: Windows' RAM rounded up to a whole GB, then less 4 (the owner, 2026-11-04, at the release gate: reported RAM is always a little under what is installed, so a PC sold as 16 GB that reports 15.4 GiB gets memory=12GB, not 11); allin1 is left out at 14 GiB or less, 11 GiB or less is refused

Release gate: the lyrics aligner's first-use download (1.26 GB) shows no progress on the page (only the lyrics stage running); its lines every 50 MB go to the job's log. Since the review of the gate fixes it goes through runtime.download_part, so it is retried, and a cut one is resumed by the next song with lyrics. The advisor on the release candidate (finding 9): one line in the lyrics stage's detail while it downloads would do; left out of v0.1 (it needs a weights check in the pipeline and its stand-ins).

Release gate: an install made before songcharter's own uv cache (runtime/uv-cache) keeps its ~/.cache/uv, which songcharter no longer counts or deletes. Its next run downloads nothing into the new cache while its environments are complete: checked with uv 0.13.5 (the pinned tarball) on a setuptools project installed --no-editable, whose re-sync with an empty cache, offline too, only 'Checked 2 packages'. A new release (the app at a new path) rebuilds songcharter's wheel, which needs setuptools: one small download (4.4 MB of cache with the index pages), plus what the new lock changes; offline that rebuild fails. v0.1 is not released, so only dev and CI installs have an old cache.

Release gate: the install's closing summary prints doctor.json as step 8 wrote it, before WSL restarts with the memory step 9 set (on a 16 GB PC with no .wslconfig, 'WSL has 7.8 GB ... allin1 is left out'). The page's header and diagnostics' doctor-now.json measure it again; the GPU is not measured again in the header. The advisor on the release candidate (finding 7) and its skeptic: on a PC that reports under about 15.2 GiB the summary also shows the problem 'WSL has 7.4 GB of memory, under 8 GB' and 'doctor: 1 problem', and install.sh exits 1 after the restart it runs (nothing is skipped; the exit code is never seen). The fix, later: when step 9 wrote .wslconfig (its flag), drop the WSL-memory problem and the two memory notes from the summary, end with 'WSL's memory is measured again after the restart', and take the exit code from the problems left. It must not hide the disk and component problems, nor the memory problem when no restart follows (.wslconfig kept, a No, or a rerun after an interrupted restart, whose 'kept' sets no flag), and plain Linux and CI (no flag) stay as they are. M4-08 records the install's last lines.

GPU smoke test: song.ogg differs between two charts of the same song only in each Ogg page's serial number and checksum (notes.chart and song.ini identical), against the rule that the same input gives byte-identical output. The Ogg muxer picks a random stream serial; a fixed one (ffmpeg's bitexact flags, to check) would make the folder byte-identical.

GPU smoke test: each guitar take's expert_job.json records executionProvider "cpu" while the take ran on CUDA (its results say cuda; the GPU was at 99%): the job file's field misleads anyone reading it.
Release gate: the test song's CPU chart (1 take) leaves guitar gaps in solos 3C-3D (about 5:45-6:15) where the stem plays; M4-08 compares the 4-take chart's preview (its 'Added at the release gate').

A guitar take that fails on CUDA is not run again on the CPU (v0.1 says what to try instead: pipeline.gpu_failed). The skeptic's option (b) on the advisor's finding 1, for v0.1.1 once M4-08 has measured the friend's free VRAM and per-take peaks: per-seed calls, the failed seed rerun with engines.guitar(..., [seed], 'cpu') and recorded as a fallback with a warning, per-take devices in pipeline.json's takes. Risks: a broad catch also retries timeouts and failures that are not CUDA's, and it puts a CPU node engine beside the parent's CUDA context inside the friend's 12 GB WSL.

The work cache's 24-hour exemption (cache.RECENT_S): a folder used in the last day is never pruned, so an evening of 10 songs keeps about 7-12 GB in work/ and ac/ past the 5 GB budget until the next day, and WSL's disk on C: does not shrink by itself when they go (the skeptic on the advisor's finding 6). The page now shows doctor's low-disk problems as they happen. Later: a 'songcharter uses N GB (cache M GB)' line or a 'free the cache' button. library/, exports/ and replaced/ stay unpruned (the friend's charts, about 6-9 MB a song).

An upgrade (0.1.0, then 0.1.1's install line over that install) is tested nowhere: CI installs one version, and install.sh removes the other app/* folders and rebuilds the wheel. Before v0.1.1: a second build in 70-release.sh, and the new line run over the old install (the advisor on the release candidate, finding 10).

Polish seen in part A: the install shows an HF Hub 'unauthenticated requests' warning, npm's deprecation and .npmignore warnings, and allin1's download bars as wide as the terminal; the ADTOF weights' download prints no 'done' line; an MP3 with no artist tag charts as 'Unknown' (the file name is not read for 'Artist - Title', and the page offers no field to fix it); the song folder's name is cut at 40 characters mid-word (cache.safe_name), and the preview's title with it.

Fast runs (seen 2026-11-05, the owner's stress test on a 9-minute shred instrumental, 4 CUDA takes): the chart's total is close to human charts' (2,137 Expert notes against 2,236 and 2,382 in two human charts of the song, from Encore's counts), but it peaks at 11 notes a second where both human charts reach 17, and runs at about 7 a second through 10-second stretches the humans chart at their peak: the guitar engine thins the fastest runs. Also: allin1 named most of the song Solo, so the solo markers cover about 7 minutes of it. Candidates for M5's quality work.

Long, busy songs lose the guitar's ending (seen 2026-11-05, the 9-minute shred instrumental): all four takes stop at 498.6 s of 544.8 s (every take's section windows from there hold 0 onsets) while the human charts have notes to about 9:00 and bass and drums run to 539 s. The cause, by its numbers: autochart's decoder has a budget of 8,192 tokens a job (the model manifest's maxTokens; ac_headless.cjs logs 'decoder used its whole ... tokens'), and this song used it up after about 2,190 notes. songcharter neither splits a long song's transcription (overlapping chunks, then stitched) nor tells the user that the guitar ended early. A dense 5-minute song may reach it too. The scorer against two human charts (in the scratch folder, not committed): onsets within 100 ms, 71-73% of the human notes found and 76-79% of ours in theirs (the two human charts agree at 91-96%); about 92% found in the slow first two minutes, 47% in passages at 8-12 notes a second; exact fret agreement 23-27% (the humans with each other 46%); timing of matched notes within 10 ms of the community chart; chord, HOPO, tap and sustain shares near the community chart's; our tempo map at double the humans' (beats aligned: octave-tolerant beat F1 0.94-0.96).
